approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic algorithm over molecular graphs with a surrogate deciding which offspring get bought. Each session starts from ten scored molecules and keeps every accepted observation as its only label source. A breeding population holds the 64 highest-scoring molecules seen so far; breeding parents are drawn from the top score quantiles (the best tenth takes 60% of draws, the next quarter 30%, the next half 10%, so only the better-scoring half ever breeds). Offspring come from seven graph mutation families plus a connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing mutation, under a sulfur-introduction gate, a canonical-identity admission check and two duplicate scopes. For every announced batch of ten the generator breeds a fresh pool of 160 candidates, fits a Gaussian process on this session's accepted scores alone (Morgan count fingerprints, Tanimoto-style kernel) and picks ten by correlated Thompson sampling. The mechanism this Anchor itself added is a stall rule: after three consecutive announced batches with no new best, only the forty highest posterior means of the pool stay eligible until the first improving batch restores the full field. Survivor membership is the one stage of this algorithm that the whole of the last exploration window left untouched: the population is still chosen by score alone, so once the search finds a good decorated scaffold its slots fill with near-identical siblings of it.
approach.novelty: Survivor membership becomes niche-elite instead of score-greedy. The population still holds at most 64 records in the same score order, but at most one per shape class, where a shape class is the molecule's own graph with every element label and every bond order erased - one carbon skeleton per topology. A halogen ladder, a heteroatom permutation or a nitroso/thiocarbonyl swap therefore keeps only its best-scoring member and the freed slot goes to a topologically different molecule, while the best record ever accepted is always kept. Nothing else moves: the quantile sampler, the operator mixture, the pool, the surrogate, the Thompson draw and the stall mask are untouched, so the arm isolates which records survive. The two sibling arms of this round change the surrogate's uncertainty model and the stall mask's release rule, and neither touches the population. Two earlier attempts in this lineage did touch diversity-aware retention and both lost: one partitioned by molecular mass and lipophilicity cells and simultaneously replaced parent sampling by uniform draws over cell champions, which occupied at most 41 of its 64 cells, cut mean offspring score from 0.3720 to 0.2898 and lost 0.055 on the panel; the other grouped by ring-system core and refilled all 64 slots core by core on a much older version of this algorithm, where the protected records landed below the quantiles that actually breed and none of 602 of them ever bred. This arm keeps score pressure exactly as it is, bounds the archive at the inherited capacity so the sampler's band geometry is unchanged, and puts the partition on the axis where this panel's own receipts show the waste is - element permutations of one topology that the objectives score identically - so the records it deletes are the leader's near-duplicate siblings inside the bands that do the breeding, not weak strangers below them.

observed_bottleneck: The behaviour that limits the Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d is where its scaffold lock is enforced: the global score-greedy top-64 survivor truncation fills the breeding population with element-permutation siblings of the current leader, so the parents the inherited quantile sampler can actually reach stop being distinct chemistry long before the budget ends. Read-only reconstruction of this Anchor's own fifteen published sessions (4,350 accepted records; its own trajectories under its node directory) measures the redundancy directly: of 290 accepted records per session only 109-245 are distinct once element identity and bond order are erased from the graph, 85-225 of the 290 sit in a class with at least one other record, the largest class holds 7-43 records, and 543 of the 7,773 within-class score pairs are equal to within 1e-9. Replaying the inherited retention rule over those same streams, the support the score-quantile sampler can draw from (the ranks covered by edges 0.10/0.25/0.50) averages 18.86 distinct skeletons and 7.86 distinct generic Murcko frameworks, and the 0.6-weight top band holds only 4.81 distinct skeletons among about 6.4 members; the final 64 survivors span 4-40 distinct Murcko frameworks (mean 15.8) and the last hundred accepted records of a session put 22-86% (mean 53%) of their evaluations on one generic framework. The lineage has watched this survive everything but retention: h-15de06b0081a7af2 records the lock surviving a changed proposal supply, two reserved-allocation quotas and a full-coverage in-generator refinement stage; in n-82195b802723 every seed locks onto one analogue series within 60-150 evaluations, with 530 proposals repeating an earlier proposal's exact score and six halogen analogues all scoring 0.4478; in n-8b078abdc05d 9-58% of each session's last hundred proposals sit within Tanimoto 0.6 of the running best with top-thirty sets spanning 2-5 generic frameworks; n-eaa24506506e shows breadth is not the lever (-0.055666 and 36% of its first-third increment mass lost when the fresh field was cut a quarter); and this Anchor's own molecular review finds seven molecules tying at exactly 0.438799 that differ only in F/Cl/Br substitution and in which ring position takes the pyridyl nitrogen. The arithmetic that makes this matter is that realized gain is early: recomputed on this Anchor's own streams, 3.740944 of its 5.978073 whole-run increment mass (62.6%) falls in the first ten announced batches (the mask-free Parent n-1744a1494180 totals 5.819415), which is what sank the uniform quotas (h-bafdbfa51e5aa263) and what a retention rule, unlike a quota, acts on directly.

adoptions.applicability: This lineage is a GB-GA-derived loop whose retention is exactly the global greedy-64 top-k the source replaces, and its own receipts match the diagnosis quantitatively: 85-225 of each session's 290 accepted records share an element-permutation class, 543 within-class score pairs are exactly equal, and the sampler-reachable support averages only 18.86 distinct skeletons. The adoption is therefore the retention principle alone, applied to this Anchor's accepted-only archive; the source's efficiency and success-ratio advantage, its 100-run rediscovery budget and its explicit tie on maximum-median benchmarks are context only, so median_2 is not expected to carry this arm's effect and the endpoint claim rests on this campaign's own fifteen-cell panel.

literature_review.conclusion: The ticket's frozen basis is the round-44 bottleneck review, reused here through its review id; this node carries only that review's niche-retention and diversity-ranking sources and re-read the primary GB-EPI text at the cited URL to fix the exact rule before adopting it. The text supplies three things and withholds a fourth: the retention principle (best evaluated solution per niche, replacing the graph-GA family's global top-k), the diagnosis this lineage matches (a concentrated, highly self-similar, nearly score-identical population), its own evidence boundary (efficiency, success ratio and diversity at a 100-run rediscovery budget, with an explicit tie on maximum-median-molecule tasks, so median_2 is not expected to carry the effect), and no usable parameterization: its niches are a pre-declared mass/log P tessellation and its parent rule is unstated. The campaign's own measurements therefore bound the design rather than the paper's defaults. Fixed physicochemical cells coupled to uniform champion breeding were already tested on this lineage and lost 0.055187 with its constituents unseparated, and the coarser ring-system-core retention is Knowledge-only at -0.029690 because its protected records never reached the sampled quantile bands; this Anchor's own accepted streams show where the waste actually is (85-225 of 290 records per session in an element-permutation class, 543 exactly equal within-class score pairs, only 4.81 distinct skeletons in the top band that takes 60% of first-parent draws). So the partition is bound to the element-and-bond-order-blind whole-molecule skeleton, the capacity and the sampler are left exactly as inherited, and the predicted direction is internal: the freed slots are inside the bands that breed. Literature origin is not permission to continue - one complete exposed panel ends this recipe, and if the partition applies exactly while realized increment mass does not rise, the population-concentration premise is recorded as refuted for this Anchor with no sweep of feature, resolution or capacity.

method_change.previous_method: Global score-greedy top-64 truncation of the accepted-only survivor population, with score-quantile parent sampling over it.
method_change.proposed_method: Niche-partitioned elite retention: at most one accepted record per element-and-bond-order-blind whole-molecule skeleton, the best-scoring member, bounded by the same 64-member capacity and handed to the same score-quantile sampler in the same order.
method_change.rationale: This is the window's declared external break-in on retention, adopting the published graph-GA MAP-Elites retention principle into one component of the Anchor. Retention membership is the stage the previous window never touched while the scaffold lock survived four other interventions (h-15de06b0081a7af2), and the Anchor's own streams show its slots filling with element-permutation siblings of the leader: only 4.81 distinct skeletons in the top band that takes 60% of first-parent draws, 543 exactly equal within-class score pairs. The component scope is deliberate - the generator, the allocator, the mask and the sampler are untouched - so the result is attributable to membership alone.

hypothesis: Remove within-niche redundancy from the retained breeding population. Retention keeps at most one accepted record per niche - the highest-scoring member, earliest serial on ties - where a record's niche is the canonical form of its own molecular graph with every atom mapped to carbon and every bond to a single bond, computed from the graph alone. Niche elites then compete for the inherited 64-member capacity in the inherited (-score, serial) order and are handed to the untouched score-quantile sampler in that order, so the accepted incumbent is always retained and the population stays bounded exactly as before. Path of effect: the slots that currently hold element-permutation siblings of the leader are freed for topologically distinct accepted records; because the removed records are the leader's own near-duplicates rather than weak distant molecules, the freed slots sit inside the bands the sampler actually draws from, so each announced batch is bred from more distinct chemistry at a near-unchanged parent score level, which is the condition under which the rare large early increments this panel's endpoint depends on can appear.

finding_summary.headline: Niche-elite retention applied exactly and bought the forecast diversity, but increment mass fell 11.8% and the panel lost 0.047: premise refuted
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment did what a clean falsification should. Score-greedy truncation really was filling this Anchor's breeding bands with element permutations of the leader, the fix removed them exactly as designed, the freed slots really did land inside the bands the sampler draws from, and the parents that bred really were more skeleton-diverse at nearly unchanged score - and the panel's realized gain still fell. That is the registered premise test, not an implementation failure, so the population-concentration explanation of this lineage's endpoint ceiling is now refuted for this Anchor, and the route stops on its own condition: no sweep of niche feature, resolution or capacity is licensed, which closes the partition-redefinition follow-up as well as this configuration.

Two measurements explain why more distinct chemistry bought nothing, and both point away from the population. First, the key counted decoration, not chemistry. The 10.15 extra skeletons the rule put into the sampler-reachable support bought only 1.08 extra typed Murcko ring systems and 2.88 extra generic frameworks, a ratio of about nine new skeletons per new ring system, and the 0.6-weight top band still spans under three generic frameworks among its 6.4 members (Parent 2.57). The molecular review's independent read of the same streams finds the same thing from the other side, 40 distinct skeletons collapsing onto 7 generic frameworks in one top decile with one framework taking 36.8% of the band. Erasing element labels and bond orders makes moving a pendant halogen from a ring carbon to an amide nitrogen a new niche while leaving the ring system untouched, so the archive was partitioned largely by where the decoration sits. Second, and more decisive, the proposal stage converted the richer population straight back into indistinguishable spend: exactly equal accepted-record scores stayed flat at 601 against the Parent's 622, and the molecular review finds elite bands where only 33 to 84 of the top 87 proposals have distinct scores at all. The budget is being spent on edits the objectives cannot resolve regardless of which parents are available, and the timing signature confirms it - the richer population was consumed earlier (76.2% of all increment mass in the first ten batches, up from 62.6%) and then stalled harder, rather than sustaining later gains.

So the search behaviour that limits this method is move granularity, not membership. The operator mixture performs sustained local refinement of whatever scaffold it starts on - single-atom and pendant edits, plus a crossover whose products stay inside the inherited ring systems - and no retention rule, acquisition quota or ranking term can make such a move set produce the rare large increments this endpoint needs. Two earlier arms on this lineage already failed on the supply and quota sides and this one fails on the membership side, which is three independent stages exhausted on the same premise. The class of method the evidence now points to is a proposal operator that changes what the molecule is: fragment- or ring-system-level moves (scaffold replacement, fragment-library recombination, whole-substituent installation and removal) together with a novelty or duplicate key read at ring-system granularity rather than on the decorated whole-molecule graph, so that one proposal differs from its parent by an amount the objective can resolve. This also weakens, without testing, the route's reserved acquisition-side diversity-ranking successor: diversity entered the ranking that matters here through the population and was used, and the conversion still failed, so a ranking term inherits the same conversion problem. A secondary limitation worth naming is that the inherited quantile edges reach only ranks 0-31 of the 64-member archive at a mean parent topness of 0.94, so the lower half of the niche archive - exactly its most topologically distant records - is never bred from; the published source's own escape route, breeding from distant niches, was deliberately not adopted here, and the one lineage test of uniform champion access lost 0.055, so any access-side variant has to be rank-aware rather than uniform. The surrogate is not implicated: within-batch prediction-to-score rank correlation was 0.526 here against 0.515 in the Parent and chronological prediction error was slightly better, so roughly half the within-batch ordering is uninformative in both arms and this node did not change it. What remains open is attribution of the score loss rather than of the mechanism: the deco_hop seed-0 departure accounts for about a third of the panel delta, the whole delta lies inside the registered path-noise band, and sitagliptin_mpo's loss on all three seeds - concentrated entirely in batches 11 to 29 while its early mass rose on two of the three - is not explained by any quantity measured here.
finding_summary.results:
The retention rule ran exactly as registered in all 4,350 accepted retention calls of the fifteen sessions. No call ever retained two records of one skeleton, none exceeded the inherited 64-member capacity, the maximum accepted score was present and first in the population after every call, and the key never fell back to a record's own identity (0 of 4,500 keys); all 4,350 newcomer keys recompute from the published trajectories without a single mismatch. The partition was active and nowhere near degenerate: 1,564 of 4,350 calls (35.95%, against a forecast 38.0%) placed the newcomer in an already occupied skeleton, 1,470 records were deleted as within-niche non-elites that the passive same-state greedy-64 comparator would have kept (67 to 150 per session, forecast 54 to 187), the population averaged 55.3 to 58.8 of its 64 slots (forecast 55.4 to 58.7) and reached the full 64 in 15 of 15 sessions, and occupancy never collapsed below the ten skeletons of the initial cohort. Divergence from the Parent begins exactly where the mechanism predicts and nowhere earlier: every session reproduces the Parent's molecules evaluation for evaluation up to the first announced batch bred after the first within-niche deletion, at evaluation 21, 31, 41 or 51 of 300, and the whole eight-hunk change is confined to retention and its receipts, with pool width, the single ten-by-one-hundred-sixty normal draw per batch and its consumption, the jitter ladder, zero posterior fallbacks, the sulfur gate, both duplicate scopes and the K=3 / M=40 stall mask all behaving identically to the Parent in all 435 batches.

The two intermediate diversity observables moved as forecast. In the ranks the inherited quantile edges can actually draw, distinct skeletons rose from a Parent-replay 19.05 to 29.20 (forecast 28.80) and distinct generic Murcko frameworks from 7.85 to 10.73 (forecast 11.19); in the 0.6-weight top band distinct skeletons rose from 4.83 to 6.38 (forecast 6.31) at a top-band mean-score cost of 0.010 (0.4658 to 0.4554, forecast 0.4549). The breeding parents actually used carried that diversity: per session 74.5 distinct skeletons and 28.3 distinct generic frameworks among the parents of the 290 accepted offspring, against the Parent's 59.4 and 23.3, at a near-unchanged mean first-parent score (0.4470 against 0.4558) and unchanged topness. Late-session concentration fell on the mean, the single most common generic framework over a session's last hundred accepted records dropping from 0.533 to 0.411, but its spread widened to 0.10-0.96 against the Parent's 0.22-0.86, with one session putting 96% of its last hundred records on one framework. Final survivors spanned 21.1 typed Murcko ring systems (Parent 15.8) and 17.3 generic frameworks (Parent 9.0).

The benefit did not follow. Summed best-so-far increment mass over the fifteen cells fell from the Anchor's 5.978073 to 5.269884, a loss of 0.708189 (11.8%), with 245 incumbent improvements against 253. The early mass the intent asked to protect actually rose, 3.740876 to 4.014261, so the loss is entirely later: batches 11-20 fell from 1.586726 to 1.022236 and batches 21-29 from 0.650471 to 0.233387, and the stall mask fired in 97 of 435 batches against 88. Per-evaluation offspring quality did not degrade at all (mean accepted offspring score 0.3809 against 0.3782, median 0.4137 against 0.4117, parent-beating accepted records 673 against 634), which separates this arm cleanly from the earlier physicochemical-champion arm that halved offspring quality. The endpoint panel fell: child macro mean 0.559818 against 0.607030, paired delta -0.047213 with all three seeds negative (-0.107912, -0.018696, -0.015029), against a registered minimum effect of +0.002. By task, zaleplon_mpo +0.017877 and drd2_docking +0.011548 held their 0.02 and 0.03 margins, median_2 moved +0.005691 and stayed inside its registered band as the source's own tie predicted, deco_hop lost 0.078274 and sitagliptin_mpo lost 0.192905 on all three seeds. The deco_hop loss is the documented departure cell: seed 0 realized 0.623961 instead of the inherited 0.856148, worth about -0.0155 of the fifteen-cell mean, and the panel delta of -0.047213 sits inside the registered ungated law-free reference band, which would place it below that reference only under -0.050871. Every cell completed with 1,500 oracle calls, status ok, no timeout and no invalid or duplicate proposal; the registered per-key cost held at 0.44 ms for the retention key and 1.06 ms for all three cached labels, about 0.3 s per session.

So the search behaviour that limits this method is move granularity, not membership. The operator mixture performs sustained local refinement of whatever scaffold it starts on - single-atom and pendant edits, plus a crossover whose products stay inside the inherited ring systems - and no retention rule, acquisition quota or ranking term can make such a move set produce the rare large increments this endpoint needs. Two earlier arms on this lineage already failed on the supply and quota sides and this one fails on the membership side, which is three independent stages exhausted on the same premise. The class of method the evidence now points to is a proposal operator that changes what the molecule is: fragment- or ring-system-level moves (scaffold replacement, fragment-library recombination, whole-substituent installation and removal) together with a novelty or duplicate key read at ring-system granularity rather than on the decorated whole-molecule graph, so that one proposal differs from its parent by an amount the objective can resolve. This also weakens, without testing, the route's reserved acquisition-side diversity-ranking successor: diversity entered the ranking that matters here through the population and was used, and the conversion still failed, so a ranking term inherits the same conversion problem. A secondary limitation worth naming is that the inherited quantile edges reach only ranks 0-31 of the 64-member archive at a mean parent topness of 0.94, so the lower half of the niche archive - exactly its most topologically distant records - is never bred from; the published source's own escape route, breeding from distant niches, was deliberately not adopted here, and the one lineage test of uniform champion access lost 0.055, so any access-side variant has to be rank-aware rather than uniform. The surrogate is not implicated: within-batch prediction-to-score rank correlation was 0.526 here against 0.515 in the Parent and chronological prediction error was slightly better, so roughly half the within-batch ordering is uninformative in both arms and this node did not change it. What remains open is attribution of the score loss rather than of the mechanism: the deco_hop seed-0 departure accounts for about a third of the panel delta, the whole delta lies inside the registered path-noise band, and sitagliptin_mpo's loss on all three seeds - concentrated entirely in batches 11 to 29 while its early mass rose on two of the three - is not explained by any quantity measured here.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic molecules; one genuinely drug-like amine/phenol family, elsewhere elites built on N-F, nitroso, peroxide and thioacyl-halide bonds
molecular.overall_character: Across all five streams the generator proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task over three seeds (4350 total), every one RDKit-parsable, mean 24-33 heavy atoms, 3.1-4.7 rings and 2.2-3.7 aromatic rings, with digest ring_closure_rate 0.962-0.985 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.954-0.983. So the ring and aromatic chemistry is real and plentiful; the problem is what hangs off it. Four of the five streams carry a halogen in 86-97% of proposals (digest halogen_rate 0.9103, 0.923, 0.9713, 0.2345, 0.8575), and the score-leading band is dominated by bonds that do not exist in practice: an RDKit read of the trusted trajectories finds at least one heteroatom-halogen, peroxide, hydrazine, N-O or nitroso bond in 96.6% and 69.0% of the top-decile proposals of two streams, against 5.8%, 46.0% and 70.1% in the other three. Nothing anywhere carries a formal charge (digest charged_rate 0.0 on all five) and nothing anywhere carries a specified stereocentre (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five), while 52-97% of the molecules in three streams contain at least one undefined stereocentre. On the node's own registered diversity question, read as molecule counts only and left to analyze to judge: distinct element-and-bond-order-blind whole-molecule skeletons in the proposal stream rose against the Parent on four of five tasks (431 vs 362, 620 vs 600, 578 vs 562, 436 vs 417) and fell on one (625 vs 657); distinct generic Murcko frameworks rose on three (93 vs 70, 246 vs 202, 124 vs 102) and fell on two (199 vs 241, 357 vs 380); and the single most common generic framework among each seed's last hundred proposals fell on 12 of 15 seed-task windows and rose on 3, one sharply (0.96 against the Parent's 0.42). The added skeletons are mostly decoration placements, not new ring systems: in one stream's top decile 40 distinct skeletons collapse onto 7 generic frameworks.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals per three seeds, digest mean SMILES length 44.0, ring_closure_rate 0.9839, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9828, halogen_rate 0.9103. RDKit read: mean 24.1 heavy atoms, 3.09 rings, 2.62 aromatic rings, 92.4% with two or more aromatic rings, 85% containing an amide. The run converged on one decorated core, an ethyl/methoxy-substituted 5,6-fused indole-type tricyclic 2-carboxamide with an N-aryl amide, seen in the best-of-run CCc1c2cc3c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c4ccccc4)n3C2)c1OC (0.4801, C19H17FN2O2) and in all twelve digest best molecules. The top decile holds 40 distinct element-blind skeletons but only 7 generic Murcko frameworks, one of them 36.8% of it.
liabilities: N-haloamides and N,N-dihaloanilines in 68% of the top decile, groups with no practical existence: CCc1c2cc3c(cc(C(=O)Nc4cccc(N(F)Cl)c4)n3C2)c1OC and CCc1c2cc3c(cc(C(=O)Nc4cccc(N(Cl)Br)c4)n3C2)c1OC both at 0.4691.
N-chloro hydrazides at the same score: CCc1c2cc3c(cc(C(=O)N(NCl)c4cccc(F)c4)n3C2)c1OC.
14 proposals under 6 heavy atoms, including the digest worst molecules ClBr, BrBr and Br at 0.0, appearing as late as evaluation 280.
Partially dearomatized tautomer forms in the final batch, e.g. C=CC1=C(C)C=c2[nH]c(C(CO)N(Br)c3ccccc3)cc2=C(CS)O1 at 0.1098, which mix aromatic and quinoid notation on one ring.
missing_features: A halogen-free C/H/N/O composition: 91% of proposals carry a halogen and the best-of-run is C19H17FN2O2, one pendant fluorine away from an all-CHNO isomer, so the family never presents the halogen-free composition that the plateau would need to test.

Nitriles: exactly 1 nitrile in 870 proposals, although the initial pool contained one (COc1cc(OC)c2c(-c3cccc(-c4ccc(C#N)cc4)c3)cc(=O)oc2c1), so the operator can delete that group but never install it.
An N-alkyl acetamide on an azine-fused azole in place of the carbon-rich indole anilide: every digest best keeps the inherited core and varies only its decoration.
Basic amine centres: only 42 of 852 proposals carry a ring basic nitrogen, and no piperidine or piperazine appears at all in 870.
Any specified stereochemistry: digest stereocentre_rate 0.0.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: High and low differ by decoration of a fixed core, not by the core. Over the 852 proposals of 10 or more heavy atoms, molecules with an N-halogen bond average 0.359 against 0.302 without; an amide is +0.082 and an aromatic ring nitrogen +0.057; an aryl fluoride is -0.031 and a phenol -0.049. 68% of the top decile carries an N-halogen bond and 33% an N-N bond. The gradient is also saturated: six digest best molecules differing only in which halogen pair sits on one nitrogen (N(F)Cl, N(F)Br, N(Cl)Br, N(Cl)Cl) all return exactly 0.4691434622489256, and the best member of the same core with no N-halogen bond, CCc1c2cc3c(cc(C(=O)Nc4cccc(Br)c4)n3C2)c1OC, reaches 0.4464. The whole climb from the best initial molecule COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC at 0.3051 to 0.4801 is bought by substituent edits on an inherited indole-2-carboxamide.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, digest mean SMILES length 58.7 with a 174-character maximum, ring_closure_rate 0.9759, halogen_rate 0.923. RDKit read: mean 32.6 heavy atoms, 4.03 rings, 3.71 aromatic rings, 96.8% with two or more aromatic rings, mean QED 0.292, the lowest of the five streams. Nine digest best molecules share that one framework at the identical score 0.6331.
liabilities: Thioacyl fluorides, C(F)=S, in 64.4% of the top decile and 14.8% of the whole stream, a group absent from the Parent's proposals entirely (0 of 870).
Bis-nitroso arenes in 19.2% of proposals and 64.4% of the top decile, e.g. CC(N=O)(Nc1cc(SF)c(N=O)cn1)c1c(OCCl)c(C(F)=S)c(C(F)=S)c2ccsc12.
Chloromethyl and chloroperoxy ethers: OCCl in the best-of-run and OOCl in O=Nc1cnc(NC(N=O)c2c(OOCl)c(C(F)=S)c(F)c3c2SC=CC3)cc1F at 0.6342; peroxides in 23.6% of the stream.
19 proposals under 6 heavy atoms, including C#C, CCl, F and ClCOCl, each collecting the 0.5 floor rather than information.
missing_features: A sulfonamide or sulfone linker: zero sulfonamides and zero sulfones in 870 proposals, although the initial pool contained an aryl sulfonamide.

Amide linkages between the two ring systems: only 21 of 848 proposals contain an amide, and they average 0.549 against 0.597 for those without, so the generator has no way to test an amide-linked decoration.

Nitriles as a polar end group: 30 of 870 here, where the Parent's runs on the same objective proposed 257.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scored range is narrow and floored: the digest worst molecules CCl, F and ClCOCl all sit at exactly 0.5, the median is 0.5987 and the best 0.6409, so almost all signal lives in a 0.1 band. Within it the rewarded edits are exotic: over the 848 proposals of 10 or more heavy atoms a thioacyl halide is +0.024, a nitroso +0.022 and an O-halogen +0.018, while a phenol is -0.024 and an amide -0.048. In the top decile 64.4% carry a nitroso group, 64.4% a C(=S)-halogen, 63.2% an O-halogen and 34.5% a peroxide. The best molecule free of all such bonds, Cc1nc(Nc2ncnc3c(C(F)F)c(C(C)C=O)ccc23)c2nnc(C(C)(C)C)c(CF)c2n1, reaches 0.6240, so the last 0.017 of the climb is paid for entirely in non-existent functional groups.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, digest mean SMILES length 54.5, ring_closure_rate 0.9793, halogen_rate 0.9713. RDKit read: mean 31.0 heavy atoms, 4.59 rings, 2.18 aromatic rings. This is the one stream whose elites look like ordinary medicinal chemistry: 87.0% of proposals carry a basic amine, 66.5% a ring basic nitrogen, 58.4% a phenol, and only 5.8% of the top decile carries any heteroatom-halogen, peroxide or nitroso bond, with a top-decile mean QED of 0.617, the highest of the five. The top decile spans 34 generic frameworks, the broadest elite band of the five streams.
liabilities: Cyclopropa-fused benzenes in two of the three 1.0-scoring molecules: the c3cc4c5c(F)c3C5C4 unit in COc1cc(F)cc(CCN2CCCC(c3cc4c5c(F)c3C5C4)CC2)c1 and CC(c1cc(O)cc(F)c1)N1CCCC(c2cc3c4c(F)c2C4C3)CC1 is a pair of fused four-membered rings with four bridgehead atoms, which no chemist would call makeable.

A peroxide inside a final-batch elite: NCC1Oc2c3ccc(OO)c2C1C3NCC1CCN1Cc1cc(N)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.9834.
18 proposals under 6 heavy atoms, including the single atoms Cl and F and the pairs FF and ClCl.
N-chloro amides among the early proposals, e.g. O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0002.

The common basic heterocycles: zero piperazines and only 9 piperidines in 870 proposals, so the rewarded basic nitrogen is usually an azetidine or a ring-fusion secondary amine instead.
A catechol or meta-dihydroxy aryl pair: phenols are frequent but almost always single, so the strongest scoring feature is never doubled.
Any ionizable form: digest charged_rate 0.0, so the protonated amine that the reward appears to be reading is never expressed explicitly.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is the classic cationic-amine plus aryl-hydroxyl pharmacophore and the search found it. Over the 851 proposals of 10 or more heavy atoms, a phenol is worth +0.362 in mean score, a primary amine +0.302, a ring basic nitrogen +0.270 and a thiol +0.179, while an amide is -0.599 and an aryl fluoride -0.321. The span 0.000167 to 0.999993 is by far the widest of the five, and 84 of the top 87 proposals have distinct scores, so here the objective can still resolve the generator's edits.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, digest mean SMILES length 55.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9851 and halogen_rate 0.2345, the only stream that is not halogen-saturated. RDKit read: mean 32.3 heavy atoms, 4.65 rings, 2.44 aromatic rings, 80.8% with an amide, mean QED 0.563. The elite family is a 2-propyl-4-ethoxy biphenyl or a 2-propylquinoline ether attached to a fused piperazine-2,5-dione / diazepane-dione bicycle: CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2ccccc2C2CCN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C3=C(F)N2)c1 at 0.2421. 43.2% of proposals contain a ring of eight or more atoms and 40.5% a bridgehead atom, so these are large, saturated, polycyclic amide-rich molecules rather than flat aromatics.
liabilities: N-N single bonds in 24.6% of proposals and 33.3% of the top decile, e.g. CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2ccccc2C2CCCN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(CC)C3=NN2)c1 at 0.2387.
N-O single bonds in 13.2% of proposals and 10.3% of the top decile, including the N-O-N chain of CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2ccccc2C2CCCN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(CC)C3=NON2)c1 at 0.2372.
A cumulated C=C=N in a high-scoring proposal: CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2ccccc2C2CCCN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C3=C=N2)c1 at 0.2360.
15 proposals under 6 heavy atoms, including the digest worst molecules C, O, C=C, NCF and FBr at 0.0.
missing_features: Nitriles and trifluoromethyl groups: zero nitriles and zero CF3 groups in 870 proposals, so two of the most common polar and lipophilic end groups in medicinal chemistry are unavailable to the gradient.
Piperazines as such: only 3 in 870, with the rewarded diketopiperazine always arriving fused and amide-locked rather than as a free basic diamine.
Specified stereochemistry on the 69.5% of proposals that carry an undefined stereocentre, including every one of the digest best molecules.
A genuinely different second scaffold family in the elite band: the best twelve are decoration variants of one bicyclic dione plus one biaryl, and no proposal in any seed exceeds 0.2421.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The span is 0.0 to 0.2421 with a median of 0.1935, and the top is a plateau: the digest best twelve run from 0.2357 to 0.2421 and differ from each other by one fluorine, one methyl or one ring-size step. Over the 854 proposals of 10 or more heavy atoms an amide is worth +0.034, an ether +0.027 and a ring basic nitrogen +0.016, so no single group separates the field. Unlike the other streams the elite band is not collapsed, 36 generic frameworks with the largest holding 13.8% of it, which says the objective is close to indifferent to the frameworks this generator can reach rather than that the search narrowed too early.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals, digest mean SMILES length 49.2, ring_closure_rate 0.9621, halogen_rate 0.8575 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0851, the only stream with a non-trivial allene-like text rate. RDKit read: mean 26.4 heavy atoms, 3.72 rings, 2.54 aromatic rings, mean QED 0.626. The elite family is a xanthine-like pyrimidine-2,4-dione fused to a pyrrole, N-fluorinated and N-fluoroalkylated, carrying a 2-hydroxyphenyl fluoroalkyl ether: O=c1c2c(F)n(-c3cc(OCCF)ccc3O)cc2n(CF)c(=O)n1CCF at 0.5285, with the best-of-run Cn1c(=O)c(F)c(CC2C=NC=C2S)n(C2=CC(F)C=C2O)ccn(F)c1=O at 0.5419 built on a nine-membered ring. One seed's proposals sit on a single generic framework for 80.7% of the whole run and 96% of its last hundred; the stream's unique_molecules count, 871 of 900 read, is the lowest of the five.
liabilities: N-fluorinated amides and ring nitrogens in two-thirds of the elites, e.g. the n(F) of Cn1c(=O)c(F)c(CC2C=NC=C2S)n(C2=CC(F)C=C2O)ccn(F)c1=O and the n1F of O=c1c2c(F)n(-c3cc(OCCF)ccc3O)cc2n(CF)c(=O)n1F.
N-fluoromethyl and N-fluoroalkyl aminals, n(CF) and n1COF, as in O=c1c2c(F)n(-c3cc(OCCF)ccc3O)cc2n(CF)c(=O)n1COF at 0.2376, which would hydrolyse on contact with water.
A nine-membered ring in the best-of-run, and 25.6% of proposals with a ring of eight or more atoms against 1.95% in the Parent's proposals.
30 proposals under 6 heavy atoms, the most of any stream, including the digest worst molecules F and O at 0.0 and a 1,2-dioxetane in the trajectory.
Duplicated-fragment dimers with cumulated double bonds scoring exactly 0.0, e.g. CC(=O)C1=CC=C(O)C(n2cc3c(c2C2=CC=C=C2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3-c2c3cc(C(C)=O)cc2n2c(C4=CC=C=C4)c4c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c4c32)=CC1.
missing_features: A primary aliphatic amine: only 2.6% of proposals carry any basic amine and 0.9% a ring basic nitrogen, against 25.5% and 23.8% in the Parent's proposals on the same objective, and there are zero beta-amino amides in 870.

A trifluorinated aromatic ring: zero proposals carry three fluorines on one ring and only 2 carry a trifluoromethyl group, although 58.3% carry a single aliphatic C-F, so fluorine is added one atom at a time and never as a group.
A fused triazole or other saturated-fused diazine amine: zero triazoles and zero piperazines in 870 proposals.
Specified stereochemistry, although 54.1% of proposals contain an undefined stereocentre and the Parent's stream likewise had none.

Amide chemistry in general: 2.9% of proposals carry an amide and they average 0.050 against 0.203 for those without, so the generator has effectively abandoned the one linker class its highest-rewarded region would need.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The span runs from 4.4e-34 to 0.5419 with a median of 0.1575, and the rewarded edits are fluorine placement and a free phenol: over the 829 proposals of 10 or more heavy atoms an aryl fluoride is worth +0.054, an O-halogen +0.057, an ether +0.029 and a phenol +0.022, while an amide is -0.153. 66.7% of the top decile carries an N-halogen bond. The climb is a repeated reshuffle of two to four fluoroalkyl groups around one fused dione core: the digest best three, differing only in whether each N-substituent is CF or CCF, all return exactly 0.5285, and the final batch slides back to 0.1746-0.3864 on the same core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An RDKit read of the trusted trajectories finds N-halogen bonds in 37.7% of one stream's 870 proposals and 67.8% of its top decile, and in 36.0% and 66.7% of another's; a third stream's top decile carries a nitroso group in 64.4%, a C(=S)-halogen in 64.4%, an O-halogen in 63.2% and a peroxide in 34.5%; N-N single bonds reach 33.3% and N-O single bonds 10.3% of a fourth stream's top decile. Set-wide, at least one such bond appears in 20.3% to 58.9% of proposals depending on the stream, and the best molecule free of all of them trails the overall best by 0.002 to 0.034 on three streams.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator climbs gradients by forming bonds between two heteroatoms, or between a heteroatom and a halogen, instead of by changing what the molecule is.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The candidate path needs a plausibility gate applied to bonds it creates, rejecting new heteroatom-heteroatom and heteroatom-halogen bonds that do not occur in its own reference library, or an atom-substitution table restricted to element swaps that keep every bond in a type the library contains. Without it the reward the generator follows is produced largely by groups no chemist would make, and the elite population it carries forward is unusable as chemistry regardless of score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five proposal streams, 4350 molecules, while an RDKit read of the same files finds at least one unspecified stereocentre in 12.1%, 52.2%, 54.1%, 69.5% and 97.5% of them; the three highest-scoring molecules of one stream carry two, two and three undefined centres each, so each is written as a mixture of four to eight diastereomers.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot express stereochemistry, so configuration is outside its search space entirely.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Stereo tags are being dropped somewhere between proposal construction and canonicalization. A generator that carried them through, and that could mutate a centre as an edit, would gain a dimension of variation that costs no extra evaluation and that is invisible to it today; until then any property reading on configuration is capped at whatever the unspecified form scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the 4350 proposals, nitriles appear 0, 0, 1, 2 and 30 times per stream of 870; trifluoromethyl groups 0, 0, 0, 1 and 2; piperazines 0, 0, 0, 0 and 3; triazoles 0 in all five; no proposal anywhere carries three fluorines on one aromatic ring; and sulfones appear only in the one stream whose seed molecules already contained one, 87 of 870, so the operator can delete such a group but has never been seen to build one. Meanwhile single carbon-halogen bonds appear in 7.1% to 61.2% of proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The substituent vocabulary is atom-level rather than group-level: common medicinal-chemistry groups are almost never installed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Edits should be able to attach, swap or remove a whole substituent drawn from a fixed library of common groups, not just change one atom's element. A single-atom substitution usually moves a molecule a distance the objective cannot resolve, whereas one group-level move changes polarity, lipophilicity and hydrogen-bonding together and is the kind of step a scorer can read.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Six proposals in one stream that differ only in which pair of halogens sits on a single nitrogen (N(F)Cl, N(F)Br, N(Cl)Br, N(Cl)Cl) all return exactly 0.4691434622489256; nine in another all return exactly 0.6331, differing only in which halomethyl or methoxy group occupies one position; three in a third all return exactly 0.5285, differing only in whether each of two N-substituents is CF or CCF. Only 33 of the top 87 proposals of the first stream have distinct scores, and 45, 56, 74 and 84 in the others.
transferable_gaps.gap: A large share of proposals are edits the evaluator provably cannot distinguish, so the budget buys no information.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal stream needs either a deduplication key coarser than pendant-atom identity, or an operator that changes ring systems, so that successive calls differ in a way the objective can resolve. As it stands the generator converts budget into score ties, which is the same as spending it on repeats.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each stream of 870 contains 14 to 30 proposals with fewer than 6 heavy atoms, down to single atoms (Br, F, O, C) and two-atom pairs (ClBr, FBr, BrBr, CCl, FF, ClCl), and they occur as late as evaluation 287 of 300; every one scores its stream's floor, 0.0 on three streams and the fixed 0.5 baseline on another. Heavy-atom minima are 1 on all five streams.
transferable_gaps.gap: Degenerate sub-fragments are emitted throughout the run, not only while the population is being seeded.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A minimum heavy-atom count and a single-connected-component check on the proposal path would stop roughly 2 to 3.5% of accepted evaluations going to molecules no objective can reward. The same guard also removes the degenerate parents these fragments become once they enter the population.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Distinct element-and-bond-order-blind whole-molecule skeletons rose against the Parent on four of five streams (431 vs 362, 620 vs 600, 578 vs 562, 436 vs 417) and fell on one (625 vs 657), while distinct generic Murcko frameworks rose on three (93 vs 70, 246 vs 202, 124 vs 102) and fell on two (199 vs 241, 357 vs 380). In one stream's top decile 40 distinct skeletons map onto only 7 generic frameworks, one of them 36.8% of the band: moving a pendant halogen from a ring carbon to the amide nitrogen gives a different element-blind graph with an identical ring system, whereas exchanging one halogen for another does not.
transferable_gaps.gap: Novelty measured on the whole-molecule graph counts decoration placement as new chemistry, so skeleton counts can rise while the ring-system inventory does not widen.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A diversity or retention key read on the whole-molecule graph is partly a count of how many pendant atoms are attached and where. Keying it on the ring system, or on the ring system together with a substituent count, would make the same bookkeeping reward actual scaffold change; reporting both numbers side by side would at least make it visible when only the decoration moved.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest charged_rate is 0.0 on all five streams and an RDKit read finds zero formal charges across all 4350 proposals, including in the one stream where an uncharged basic amine carries a mean score advantage of +0.270 and a primary amine +0.302.
transferable_gaps.gap: The atom vocabulary excludes charged atoms, so no ionizable or zwitterionic form is ever proposed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: N-oxides, quaternary centres, zwitterions and explicitly protonated bases are all unreachable. If charged atoms stay out of the vocabulary this should be a stated limit of the generator rather than an accident of the mutation table, because any property term that reads charge state will see only the neutral form.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
